verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a Cooley practice page saying an S-1 draft can be updated 'with a few simple prompts', which implies natural-language operation of one AI drafting tool. It is a single thin claim, it is unclear whether clients or only Cooley lawyers can use it, and the main Cooley GO document generators show no natural-language interface. missing for 10: evidence that users (not just firm lawyers) can issue natural-language commands, natural-language operation across Cooley GO generators and guidance, documentation of the prompt interface and its scope, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands
